articles.title: Ex-Tempe school employee scheduled to appear in court on voyeurism charges
articles.description: TEMPE, AZ (AZFamily) -- A former school surveillance officer is scheduled to appear in court after authorities say he downloaded footage that showed underage girls undressing at an East Valley high school. Antony Cruz, 28, is slated to be arraigned before a judge at 8:30 a.m. Thursday. District says room was not for changing Cruz, who worked as a surveillance officer for the Tempe Union High School District, allegedly gained access to cameras that were recording a room of young teen girls undressing at Corona del Sol High School. Police noted in the court paperwork that staff and students requested the cameras be turned off for privacy, but were left on and recording the room. Authorities said Cruz did not notify school staff or law enforcement of the camera exposing the girls. Instead, Cruz reportedly downloaded several videos, with at least seven showing young girls' changing in and out of their clothes. Court documents state that the room was being used temporarily as a changing room for students because the girls' locker room was closed for renovations. District officials said the space is a dance room, not a locker room, and was never designated by the district as a place for students to change clothes. During recent locker room renovations, the district said it approved a request from Corona del Sol High School to set up a separate, camera-free location for students to change. Officials said the dance room was not one of the approved locations. A security camera was installed in the room in 2024 for campus safety purposes. Parents react at school board meeting Parents who spoke at Wednesday night's school board meeting were visibly upset, wondering if their children are victims. "He's been charged with seven counts of voyeurism, but I believe from this long, almost one-month period, that there are many more counts he should be charged with, and so I ask the district please disclose this information so we can find out the full breadth of the victims," one parent said. The district has opened an internal investigation into the matter. Cruz is facing seven counts of voyeurism and is being held on a $100,000 cash-only bond. articles.title: Class action filed over Ruby Memorial hidden cameras
articles.description: MORGANTOWN - A Monongalia County woman has filed a proposed class-action lawsuit over hidden cameras found in staff bathrooms at Ruby Memorial Hospital. The plaintiff, identified in the complaint only as P.J.P., filed the complaint September 1 in Monongalia Circuit Court. West Virginia University Hospitals and West Virginia United Health System are the named defendants. "A hospital restroom should be an unquestioned sanctuary of privacy, not a crime scene with a hidden lens," Troy Giatras, one of the attorneys who filed the complaint, told The West Virginia Record. "These dedicated healthcare workers came to work to save lives, only to have their fundamental dignity violated." In the complaint, P.J.P. alleges she was a Ruby Memorial employee during the relevant period and was among workers secretly recorded in staff restroom facilities. She says the defendants failed to protect employees from hidden-camera surveillance in nonpublic staff bathrooms. She alleges the entities were negligent and grossly negligent in hiring, supervising, training and retaining employees, including former physician Lance Parks, and in maintaining a workplace protected from invasions of privacy. According to the complaint, a staff member found a hidden recording device June 26 beneath a sink in a nonpublic staff restroom at Ruby Memorial. A second device was discovered July 1 after a facilities employee responded to a clogged toilet in another nonpublic restroom, the suit says. Authorities previously said the first device contained footage of eight hospital employees who were unknowingly recorded while partially nude. The second device contained no images or other media, according to the Monongalia County Prosecutor's Office. The complaint alleges Parks "surreptitiously recorded nude and/or partially nude employees" in the nonpublic bathrooms and the defendants did not adequately protect staff members from the alleged surveillance. "While law enforcement handles the criminal conduct of Lance Parks, the civil justice system exists to hold institutions accountable for failing their duty of care," Matt Stonestreet, another attorney representing the plaintiffs, told The Record. "WVU Hospitals provided the venue, employed the physician, and assured staff their private spaces were safe. "When an institution fails to supervise its staff and conducts sweeps that miss hidden cameras right under its nose, it shares full legal and moral responsibility for the harm caused." The complaint further alleges the hospitals failed to detect the devices, including after the first camera was found. The defendants initially suspended the employee involved and later said he no longer worked at the hospital, according to reports. Parks was charged in July with eight misdemeanor counts of criminal invasion of privacy and one felony count involving the distribution and exhibition of computer-generated child pornography, according to the Monongalia County Prosecutor's Office. Investigators executed a search warrant at his home and seized computers and digital-storage devices for forensic examination. Investigators said they were continuing to examine the seized devices to determine the full scope of potential criminal conduct and identify any additional victims. The civil complaint says Parks waived his preliminary hearing and is awaiting possible indictment by the Monongalia County Prosecutor's Office. "WVU Hospitals told staff they swept the facilities and found nothing," Giatras told The Record. "Days later, plumbing backed up and a second camera was pulled from a toilet. That is not thorough security. That is negligent indifference. "Once these deeply intimate, non-consensual recordings exist, they cannot be unseen. The psychological damage follows these victims every single day." The plaintiff contends the alleged conduct was gender-based harassment and discrimination because she is a woman and asserts the cameras were installed to secretly record women "when they were the most vulnerable." The complaint accuses the defendants of invasion of privacy, breach of confidentiality, violations of the West Virginia Human Rights Act, violation of the West Virginia Constitution, negligent supervision, negligent infliction of emotional distress, violation of the West Virginia Wiretapping and Electronic Surveillance Act and negligence. "You cannot shrug off corporate responsibility by blaming one bad actor when your own policies, supervision, and facility checks completely collapsed," Giatras said. The complaint also alleges the defendants' conduct caused anxiety, humiliation, emotional distress, pain and suffering, mental anguish, loss of enjoyment of life, annoyance and inconvenience. It seeks class certification for West Virginia residents allegedly recorded in nonpublic bathroom facilities at Ruby Memorial and "any other facility" owned, operated or managed by the defendants in the state. The plaintiff and potential class seek compensatory and punitive damages, attorney fees, court costs and class certification. The lawsuit was filed by Giatras and Stonestreet of The Giatras Law Firm in Charleston. The case has been assigned to Circuit Judge Perri J. DeChristopher. Giatras said any additional victims confidentially can contact his firm for more information by texting 304-343-2900 or visiting its website. Monongalia Circuit Court case number 26-C-347

pendingReview.title: Woman Charged With Planting Cameras in Allen County War Memorial Coliseum Bathrooms
pendingReview.description: FORT WAYNE, Ind. (WOWO) -- A Pennsylvania woman is facing charges after police say seven cameras were placed inside women's bathrooms at the Allen County War Memorial Coliseum. Breanna Deane, 30, was charged with seven counts of voyeurism, a Level 6 felony. According to WANE-15, the investigation began in March 2023 after Coliseum staff discovered cameras in a women's bathroom near Section 215. Police initially collected four cameras, including one that was still taped to a toilet. The following day, three more cameras were found taped to toilets in a women's restroom near Section 216. Police reviewed footage from several of the cameras and found video showing a person wearing a green coat, black pants with white stripes, white shoes and carrying a light-colored purse. Coliseum security footage showed a woman matching that description entering and leaving the two bathrooms before sitting in Section 216, Row 17, Seat 1. Police then reviewed ticket records and determined a credit card belonging to Deane was used to purchase the ticket. Investigators later obtained a search warrant and detained Deane during a traffic stop. Police seized her cell phone, which contained a video of a Komets hockey game and messages she sent to her husband on March 10, 2023, around the same time she was seen at the Coliseum. One of the messages read, "4 in one 3 in one." An arrest warrant was eventually issued for Deane. She was booked into the Clarion County Jail in Pennsylvania and is being held while awaiting extradition to Allen County. The reason for the delay between the 2023 investigation and the filing of charges was not immediately clear.

pendingReview.title: "I saw my neighbour..." -- Lady shares shocking moment hidden camera captured her with husband
pendingReview.description: A Nigerian woman living in the UK for her master's degree has shared how a hidden camera allegedly exposed her neighbour making advances towards her husband while her younger sister was away visiting their parents. The woman said she had initially been uncomfortable leaving her younger sister to live with her husband in Nigeria, but eventually trusted them because they were family. According to her, months after relocating to the UK, a neighbour called and questioned her decision. The neighbour reportedly said she had noticed her husband and younger sister frequently leaving the house together, returning together and going shopping together. Woman sets trap after neighbour's warning The woman said the information left her worried and unable to concentrate, prompting her to seek the help of a trusted friend. She explained that her friend installed a hidden camera in the house, which allowed her to monitor what was happening remotely from the UK. The woman said the camera later captured an unexpected scene after her younger sister travelled to visit their parents. She stated that she saw her neighbour inside the house making advances towards her husband in front of the camera. Story sparks questions about trust The revelation has raised questions about trust, relationships and the assumptions people may make when they notice unusual movements around a couple's home. The woman did not disclose what happened after she discovered the alleged encounter, leaving the subsequent reaction of her husband and neighbour unclear. Her account highlights how a warning from an unexpected source led her to investigate a situation she initially feared involved her husband and younger sister, only to reportedly discover a different development.
